title: Round-robin iterator
prompt:
Build an iterator that interleaves several integer lists, handing out one value from each non-empty list in turn until every list is used up.

- Implement the class RoundRobin(lists) with next() and hasNext() (has_next in Python). The driver runRoundRobin(lists, ops) is already written: it builds one iterator and runs each op in order.
- ops is a list of strings, "next" or "hasNext". The driver returns a list with one output per op: the value for "next", true/false for "hasNext".
- Order: the first value of list 0, then of list 1, and so on, skipping lists that have run out; then the second value of each list that still has one, and so on.
- next is only called when hasNext would return true. There are 0 to 1,000 lists, up to 100,000 values in total, and each op should take O(1) time.
hints: A simple approach precomputes the whole interleaved order. Can you produce each value only when it is asked for, without scanning past empty lists?
Keep a FIFO queue of cursors, one per list that still has values left.
next pops the front cursor, reads its value, and pushes the cursor back (advanced by one) only if its list has more values. hasNext checks whether the queue is empty.

solution.explanation: A queue holds one cursor (list index, position) per list that still has values. next pops the front cursor, returns its value and re-queues the cursor at the back if that list has more values, so exhausted lists drop out automatically. hasNext is simply "is the queue non-empty".

complexity.notes: k is the number of lists; building the queue costs O(k) once. The JavaScript version uses a head index instead of shift() (which is O(n)); a real deque would also release the consumed slots.

followUps: How would you support adding a new list to the rotation while iteration is in progress?
Generalise to a weighted rotation where list i hands out w[i] values per turn.
